properties.areaDesc: Southern Seward Peninsula Coast; Interior Seward Peninsula
properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued October 27 at 3:36PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
ESFAFG

Areas of concern are between Nome and Council, particularity streams
and rivers draining the south aspects of the high elevation terrain
of the Seward Peninsula.

Rivers and streams in the Nome and Council area are already high
following rainfall over the weekend. 1-3 more inches of precipitation
are expected by the end of the week which will keep water levels
high.

No flooding is expected at this time, however residents living near
local rivers and streams should be vigilant of the potential for ice
in culverts and other stream passage structures to restrict flow
resulting water flowing over roads in affected areas.

properties.areaDesc: Alamosa, CO; Conejos, CO; Costilla, CO; Rio Grande, CO
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 27 at 5:27PM MDT until October 27 at 7:45PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding continues, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.

* WHERE...Northeastern Conejos County, West Central Costilla County,
Southeastern Rio Grande County, and Southwestern Alamosa County...

* WHEN...Until 745 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is occurring, especially in areas along
and near the Conejos River and the Rio Grande. Widespread
inundation of agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying
areas persists. Areas of standing or slow moving water will
continue over many roadways.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 526 PM MDT, Flooding was still occurring in the warning area,
especially in low-lying areas.
- Water levels continues to remain elevated within the Conejos
River near Manassa. In addition, Widespread inundation of
agriculture fields, wetlands, and other low-lying areas.
- Low lying areas in Conejos, Costilla, Rio Grande and Alamosa
counties are impacted, especially along and near the Rio Grande
and Conejos River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Heed all road closures and directives from law enforcement and local
emergency management.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING NOW IN EFFECT UNTIL 745 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Chaves, NM; Lincoln, NM
properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 27 at 5:25PM MDT until October 27 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
At 525 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing heavy
rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 3.75 inches of rain have
fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln and Western Chaves
Counties.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

Both localized and distant heavy rainfall will create sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos and over low water crossings.

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 27 at 2:56PM AKDT until October 28 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Water levels of 1 to 2 feet above the normal highest
tide line.

* WHERE...Kuskokwim Delta Coast, including Kipnuk, Kwigillingok
and Kongiganak.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM AKDT Wednesday, highest water levels
expected during each upcoming high tide through Wednesday
morning.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Steady south to southwesterly flow is
expected to continue for the Kuskokwim Delta coastline through
Wednesday morning as a series of low pressure systems track
across the Bering Sea. Coastal erosion and perhaps nuisance
flooding of low-lying areas will be possible with each upcoming
high tide due to the persistent onshore winds. Maximum water
levels will reach between 1 and 2 ft above the normal highest
tide line, including in and around Kipnuk and Kwigillingok. A
brief break in winds and elevated water levels is forecast late
Wednesday, but a second round of elevated water levels and
persistent southerly winds are forecast with the arrival of yet
another front late Thursday into Friday.
properties.instruction: Precautions should be taken to protect property.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 4:21PM MDT until October 27 at 7:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Arroyo and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
West Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 715 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 421 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause arroyo and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln and West Central
Chaves Counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

Both localized and distant heavy rainfall will create sudden and
dangerous flows in arroyos and over low water crossings.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 715 PM MDT THIS EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 27 at 2:20PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
Between 4 and 7 inches of heavy, wet, snow fell across the
Fairbanks Metro Area Monday. Warming temperatures Monday evening
into Tuesday have caused portions of that snowfall to melt,
creating many slushy areas of melting snow and pooling water.
Overnight low temperatures Tuesday night into Wednesday morning
are expected to fall into the upper teens to low 20s which will
allow much of this slush to refreeze. Slick surfaces are very
likely Wednesday morning as wet surfaces and small water puddles
freeze. Areas of heavy, wet snow will also refreeze giving the
slush a sturdier, more ice like texture. Travel may be impacted,
especially during the Wednesday morning commute.

Additional rain and snow showers are expected overnight Wednesday
into Thursday with much lighter accumulations than Monday. Less
than an inch of new snow is possible with only a few hundredths of
an inch of liquid equivalent expected.

* WHAT...High Rip Current Risk, life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...North-facing beaches of St. Thomas, and St. John.

* WHEN...through late Tuesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

11 feet. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, life-threatening rip
current.

* WHERE... For the HIGH SURF ADVISORY, the most vulnerable areas
for high surf and beach erosion include Pinones along Road 187,
Parcelas Suarez, Villas del Mar, and Villa Christiana in Loiza;
Fortuna in Luquillo; Pueblo and Tamarindo in Aguadilla; Bario
Obrero, Pueblo and Jareaito in Arecibo; Las Boca in Barceloneta;
Machuca in Manati; Puerto Nuevo in Vega Baja; Ocean Park in San
Juan; and Barrio Espinal in Aguada. For the HIGH RIP CURRENT
RISK, beaches along west to northeast Puerto Rico.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory now until 2 AM AST Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk now through Wednesday afternoon

* IMPACTS...FOR THE HIGH SURF ADVISORY, High waves that can wash
over jetties and sweep people and pets onto jagged rocks.
Rough surf may also knock you down. Large breaking waves will
result in localized beach/dune structure erosion and dangerous
swimming conditions. FOR THE HIGH RIP CURRENT RISK, rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.
properties.instruction:
A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

A High Surf Advisory means that high surf will affect beaches in
the advisory area, producing localized beach erosion and
dangerous swimming conditions.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 1 to 2 feet of

rip currents and large breaking waves in the surf zone.

* WHERE...Northern Outer Banks.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 PM EDT
Thursday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 8 PM EDT this
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore
break can throw a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom
causing neck and back injuries.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tide levels will remain high with a King
Tide Cycle in place through Thursday. The morning high tide
will be the highest of the two daily tides.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday was 6.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.9 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.9
feet on 06/13/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood

properties.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory, IN EFFECT FROM 6 PM THIS
EVENING TO 10 AM EDT WEDNESDAY.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

stop, turn around and go another way.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 27 at 6:54AM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands.

* WHEN...Until 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be through
Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal Flood
Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf develops.
The Coastal Flood Advisory may also need to be extended beyond
Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 27 at 2:54AM HST until October 29 at 5:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
A trough moving over the state will bring abundant tropical moisture
today through at least Wednesday night. Heavy rain and isolated
thunderstorms are expected to produce flash flooding, and while the
greatest flood threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all
islands are at risk.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...All main Hawaiian Islands.

* WHEN...From 6 AM HST this morning through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy showers and isolated thunderstorms with intense rain rates
are expected to develop today and continue through Wednesday
night as a trough moves over the state. While the greatest flood
threat will be focused over Oahu and Maui County, all islands are
at risk.
properties.instruction:

should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 27 at 3:33AM EDT until October 30 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate flooding during
times of high tide. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 7 to 10 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous
rip currents.

* WHERE...Northeast Florida Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Friday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued October 27 at 2:26AM EDT until October 30 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7
to 11 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 2 AM EDT Friday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
